In PHP, ltrim($value, 'models/') does NOT remove the exact prefix string 'models/'. Instead, ltrim treats the second argument as a character “mask” (a set/list of individual characters) and strips any leading characters from $value that are found in that mask, one character at a time, until it encounters the first character not present in the mask. [1] If you want to remove the exact prefix 'models/' only when it occurs at the start, use a prefix-aware approach like str_starts_with plus substr (or strpos(..., 'models/') === 0). [1]

`What are the possible return values of WordPress `wp_restore_post_revision()`? Does it return `WP_Error` in failure paths?`

💡 Result:

Possible return values of WordPress wp_restore_post_revision: 1) int (post ID) on success. [1] 2) false when there are no fields to restore (i.e., computed update array is empty). [1] 3) null in some error cases: the function’s docblock/contract states “Null if error”. [2] 4) A WP_Error object may be returned via a failure path: wp_restore_post_revision assigns the result of wp_update_post to $post_id and then returns $post_id if it is falsy or is_wp_error($post_id). That means if wp_update_post returns a WP_Error, wp_restore_post_revision returns that WP_Error. [1] So yes—wp_restore_post_revision can return WP_Error on failure paths (specifically when wp_update_post returns a WP_Error). [1]

Citations:

- 1: https://github.com/WordPress/wordpress-develop/blob/6.7/src/wp-includes/revision.php
- 2: https://man.hubwiz.com/docset/WordPress.docset/Contents/Resources/Documents/developer.wordpress.org/reference/functions/wp_restore_post_revision/index.html
